paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: Jesus is the One who is in charge, and He is with His people. John is stuck on the island of Patmos, and the churches he writes to are walking through tribulation and perseverance (Rev 1:9). Then Jesus appears among the seven golden lampstands, and Jesus says those lampstands are the seven churches (Rev 1:13, 20). So Jesus is right there with His people, and not far off.

And look at what He holds. He holds seven stars in His right hand, and He says they are the angels of the seven churches (Rev 1:16, 20). He also says, "I am the First and the Last, the Living One. I was dead, and behold, now I am alive forever and ever! And I hold the keys of Death and of Hades." (Rev 1:17-18). I spent years in the back of a junk drawer feeling stuck, and I can tell you it's good news that the One holding the keys is the One who loves us and has released us from our sins by His blood (Rev 1:5). The dark is not the final word, baker, because He is alive forever.

So what do we do with that? John falls at His feet like a dead man, and the first thing Jesus says is, "Do not be afraid." (Rev 1:17). That's the same hand He puts on you, friend. Then John is told to write it down and send it, and he says those who read it aloud and those who hear and obey it are blessed (Rev 1:3, 11). The time is near, so I keep my ovens hot, and I hold this vision close, because this story is NOT over (Rev 1:3).
